Provides high resolution with microsecond precision and uses a monotonic clock.\n\n```APIDOC\n## performance.now()\n\n### Description\nReturns a high resolution timestamp in milliseconds representing the time elapsed since `Performance.timeOrigin` (the time when navigation started in window contexts, or when the worker is run in Worker/ServiceWorker contexts).\n\n### Syntax\n```js\nperformance.now()\n```\n\n### Parameters\nNone.\n\n### Return Value\n- **DOMHighResTimeStamp** (number) - High resolution timestamp measured in milliseconds with up to microsecond precision.\n```\n\n--------------------------------\n\n### Compare Date.now() and performance.now() timestamps\n\nSource: https://github.com/mdn/content/blob/main/files/en-us/web/api/performance_api/high_precision_timing/index.md\n\nCompares the timestamp format of Date.now() against performance.now(). Use performance.now() for monotonic, high-resolution timing that is not subject to system clock skew.\n\n```javascript\nDate.now(); // 1678889977578\nperformance.now(); // 233936\n```\n\n--------------------------------\n\n### Measure elapsed time with performance.now()\n\nSource: https://github.com/mdn/content/blob/main/files/en-us/web/api/performance/now/index.md\n\nDetermines how much time has elapsed during an operation by comparing performance.now() timestamps taken before and after execution.\n\n```javascript\nconst t0 = performance.now();\ndoSomething();\nconst t1 = performance.now();\nconsole.log(`Call to doSomething took ${t1 - t0} milliseconds.`);\n```\n\n--------------------------------\n\n### performance.now()\n\nSource: https://github.com/mdn/content/blob/main/files/en-us/web/api/performance/now/index.md\n\nReturns a high-resolution timestamp representing elapsed time in milliseconds since the time origin. Its precision is coarsened depending on cross-origin isolation status to mitigate timing attacks and fingerprinting.\n\n```APIDOC\n## performance.now()\n\n### Description\nReturns a high-resolution timestamp in milliseconds representing the time elapsed since the time origin. Resolution is coarsened for security:\n- Isolated contexts: 5 microseconds\n- Non-isolated contexts: 100 microseconds\n\n### Syntax\n```js\nperformance.now()\n```\n\n### Parameters\nNone.\n\n### Return Value\nA floating-point timestamp representing the elapsed time in milliseconds.\n\n### Example\n```js\nconst t0 = performance.now();\ndoSomething();\nconst t1 = performance.now();\nconsole.log(`Call to doSomething took ${t1 - t0} milliseconds.`);\n```\n```\n\n### High precision timing > Performance.now() vs. Date.now()\n\nSource: https://github.com/mdn/content/blob/main/files/en-us/web/api/performance_api/high_precision_timing/index.md\n\nJavaScript defines {{jsxref(\"Date.now()\")}} as the number of milliseconds elapsed since the [epoch](/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Date#the_epoch_timestamps_and_invalid_date), which is defined as the midnight at the beginning of January 1, 1970, UTC. The `performance.now()` method on the other hand is relative to the {{domxref(\"Performance.timeOrigin\")}} property. For more information, see the [time origins section](#time_origins) below.\n\nJavaScript `Date` times are subject to system clock skew or adjustments. This means that the value of time may not always be monotonically increasing. The main purpose of `Date` objects is to display time and date information to the user and so many operating systems run a daemon which regularly synchronizes time. It might be that the clock is tweaked a few milliseconds several times per hour.\n\nThe `performance.now()` method (and all other `DOMHighResTimeStamp` values) provide monotonically increasing time values and aren't subject to clock adjustments. This means that it is guaranteed `DOMHighResTimeStamp` values will be at least equal to, if not greater than, the last time you accessed it.\n\nFor measuring performance, calculating precise frame rates (FPS), animation loops, etc., use monotonically increasing high resolution time available with {{domxref(\"Performance.now()\")}} instead of JavaScript's {{jsxref(\"Date.now()\")}}.\n\nTo summarize:\n\n| -                        | {{domxref(\"Performance.now()\")}}      | {{jsxref(\"Date.now()\")}}          |\n| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- |\n| Resolution               | sub-millise
